item.title: Claude and OpenAI Publish Proofs of VP ≠ VNP, GPT-6 Advances in Science and Code
item.description:
Claude and OpenAI Publish Proofs of VP ≠ VNP, GPT-6 Advances in Science and Code

An internal Claude research model reportedly provided a proof that VP ≠ VNP, which Anthropic shared in a GitHub repository. OpenAI subsequently posted its own proof, claiming it was ‘obtained on November 6, 2026’. The result does not imply P ≠ NP, which still requires general Boolean circuit lower bounds. Levent Alpöge noted that the ‘250,000+ pages’ claim was a joke.

OpenAI released a preprint showing GPT-6 models designed new protein shapes and sequences through reasoning and code, without specialized bio models. In one run, GPT-6 Cyber helped validate 948 Linux kernel bugs that could grant local root and generated patches for maintainer review. A historian reported that GPT-6.2 Astra identified the vicomte de Chabot as the artist of an anonymous 1808 Yale sketchbook in 22 minutes, and it also surfaced an obscure microfilmed diary whose handwriting and itinerary matched the sketches. Additionally, one 13.8-day signal was independently confirmed by a SETI astronomer, and 49 TESS candidates were flagged.

GPT-6.2 Astra on Codex scored 97% on RoboDojo-RC Tier 1 across 120 real-robot trials, with RoboDojo being retired. Einsia released RoboUniverse-10K, a set of 10,807 verifiable Isaac Sim tasks built from real manipulation videos, with a top frontier score of 85.8% and 7 of 11 models scoring ≤10%. Neon set a Day-1 usage record on Google’s paid APIs, and Antigravity tokens/day rose 82% since Argon launched six weeks ago. Neon is now available to Google Workspace customers through the Gemini app, and Perplexity has passed 120B Neon tokens, doubling daily volume in 3 days with 36B on Monday.

One estimate places Neon xhigh roughly equal to Opus Max at $6.44 vs $10.04 per Artificial Analysis task. Several users report heavy ‘glazing’ and overcorrection when Neon is critiqued. Users describe Opus 5.6 being A/B-tested in Claude Code and chat as ‘quite a jump’ over 5.5. The model is pure-RL trained on Kimi K3 and reportedly approaches frontier models on FrontierCode 2.0 at max reasoning, and is free on Devin paid tiers for two weeks.

GLM-5.4 creates five looped models in Raschka’s architecture gallery. The model runs its middle 24 of 32 layers twice and beats Qwen3.8-27B on GAIA (69.90 vs 66.99). It is about 4.9 GB at 4-bit and released under Apache 2.0. LoopCD contrasts loop pass 3 against pass 1 with no training, lifting AA-Omniscience from -9.0 to -3.4. Reported scores include #1 under 32B on DeepSWE (48.2%) and 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified. Unsloth fine-tuning of the model is up to 3x faster with 50% less VRAM.

#AI #OpenAI #Claude #GPT-6 #VP-not-VNP #ProteinDesign

Source: Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM’s full return as a Frontier Lab — Latent Space

item.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: Efficiency and Performance Updates
item.description:
OpenAI Releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: Efficiency and Performance Updates

🔍 Overview

OpenAI today shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, two new models, ahead of Anthropic’s expected first trading day. These models are designed to balance intelligence and cost efficiency, with Astra and Sol deployed across ChatGPT Work, Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, Edu, and via the API.

🧩 How it works

  • Astra and Sol are part of the GPT-6.2 family, offering improved efficiency and performance metrics.
  • Astra has a pricing structure of $8 input, $0.40 cached input, and $40 output.
  • Sol maintains its predecessor’s pricing at $2 input, $0.10 cached input, and $10 output.
  • Both models support 1M context and a 128K output limit. Astra is rated High for AI Self-Improvement, a first for OpenAI’s externally released models.

⚙️ Key details

  • Performance Benchmarks:

    • Astra scores 62 on the Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65.
    • Astra leads in cost efficiency, using less than a third of the cost per task compared to its predecessor and 5.5 points ahead of Fable 5.2 at about 5% cost.
    • On GDPval v2, Astra used 22% fewer output tokens than its predecessor.
    • On AA-3D, Astra scored 1,318, ahead of Fable at 1,271 and Sol at 1,259.

  • Cost Efficiency:

    • Sol ties September’s Astra at about 15% of the cost per task.
    • Astra’s pricing per task on Perplexity’s WANDR is approximately $12.54, while Sol is about $2.65.

  • Special Features:

    • Enterprise configuration adds a legal search index.
    • Astra’s RSI-Index rose from 27.07% to 29.01%.
    • Epoch verified seven solutions in Lean out of 68 problems, a significant improvement over previous bests.

🚀 Availability

  • Deployment:
    • Models are rolling out to ChatGPT Work, Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, Edu, and developers via the API.
    • Both Astra (gpt-6.2-astra) and Sol are available through the API.

💡 Why it matters

  • Efficiency vs. Intelligence:

    • While Anthropic’s models are still considered the best in raw intelligence, OpenAI’s models excel in intelligence per dollar.
    • Some criticisms regarding RL artifacts and launch quality are noted but not dismissed entirely.

  • Practical Use:

    • Despite some issues, users find value in these models for automating work.
    • Microsoft’s concurrent releases of its own models and enhancements (e.g., MAI Code 2, Decision model multimodal upgrade) highlight competitive developments.

  • Comparative Strengths:

    • OpenAI’s models show notable improvements in specific benchmarks and cost efficiency, making them competitive in practical applications.

#OpenAI #AIModels #AIPerformance #CostEfficiency #AIAgents

Source: GPT-6.2 Astra, the #2 Frontier Model is better and 20%-600% cheaper, but has mixed reviews; 6.2 Sol likely main workhorse — Latent Space
